builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Selective and Hybrid-State Communication for Latent Multi-Agent Systems
summary: The method replaces natural-language message passing between agents with selective transfer of KV caches and recurrent states through a shared workspace. It costs implementation complexity, direct access to model internals, and some quality risk, including a six-point drop on HumanEval+ for SelectKV. It can fail when agents do not share compatible latent representations, when inherited context is disturbed, or when the production stack relies on third-party APIs that do not expose internal states.
rationale: The claimed gains are relevant to multi-agent efficiency, but the method depends on low-level access to model states that is usually unavailable with third-party APIs and is still impractical for many constrained production deployments.
technique: Selective latent-state communication for multi-agent systems

claims.statement: The method replaces natural-language message passing between agents with selective transfer of KV caches and recurrent states through a shared workspace. It costs implementation complexity, direct access to model internals, and some quality risk, including a six-point drop on HumanEval+ for SelectKV. It can fail when agents do not share compatible latent representations, when inherited context is disturbed, or when the production stack relies on third-party APIs that do not expose internal states.
HyLaMAS achieves 1.16-2.78x speedups relative to text-based multi-agent communication; SelectKV reduces communicated KV positions and logical KV payload by 9.7-9.9%.
